fixes.explanation: That's right. Moses says, “Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.” He doesn't leave a door cracked open for a deal. It's one of the plainest lines in the whole passage (Deuteronomy 7:2).

That's the reason given. Moses passes along God's words, and God says, “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” The "Me" is the LORD Himself. So the question is whose voice Israel's sons would end up following. Then the words say, “Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly destroy you.” (Deuteronomy 7:4)

Repeat sounds close, but it isn't Moses' word. He says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt…” He points to the great trials, the signs and wonders, and the mighty hand and outstretched arm (Deuteronomy 7:19). Saying it again is just talking. Moses wants them to keep it in their minds so the fear has nowhere to sit.
